title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E506 explains Lagrange's 'time-parameter' trick for integrating dx/√X = dy/√Y. Here Euler applies it to the rational analogue dx/X = dy/Y, where X = a+2bx+cx², Y = a+2by+cy².

On the previous page Euler sets dx/dt = X and dy/dt = Y, with q = x−y. Then q'/q = (X−Y)/(x−y) = 2b + c(x+y). Differentiating with dt constant gives x''/x' + y''/y' = X'(x)+Y'(y) = 4b + 2c(x+y), which is exactly 2q'/q. Integrating, x'y' = C q², that is XY/(x−y)² = C, an algebraic and complete integral.

§13 (this page):
- Euler adds b²−ac to both sides. He uses the identity (a+2bx+cx²)(a+2by+cy²) + (b²−ac)(x−y)² = (a+b(x+y)+cxy)².
- So the integral becomes (a+b(x+y)+cxy)/(x−y) = Δ, with Δ² = C + b² − ac.
- This relation is bilinear (degree 1 in each variable), so it solves rationally either way: y = ((Δ−b)x−a)/(Δ+b+cx) and x = (a+(Δ+b)y)/(Δ−b−cy).
- In modern terms, the flow of the Riccati-type autonomous equation x' = quadratic is a one-parameter group of Möbius transformations. The integral is the constancy of the polarised quadratic form B(x,y) = a+b(x+y)+cxy divided by x−y. Equivalently, the cross-ratio of x, y with the two roots of X is constant.

§14: Euler adds a cubic term d·x³ (the letter d here is a constant, not a differential).
- Then (X−Y)/(x−y) = 2b + c(x+y) + d(x²+xy+y²).
- And X'+Y' = 4b + 2c(x+y) + 3d(x²+y²).
- The difference gives x''/(x'dt) + y''/(y'dt) − 2q'/(q dt) = d(x−y)², which no longer integrates. So the trick works only up to quadratics.

§15 begins the claim that once the degree exceeds 2 no algebraic integral is possible at all. The next page illustrates this with 1+x³, where logarithms and arctangents are mixed.
errors: All algebra on the page checks: the perfect-square identity, the formulas for y and x in terms of Δ, and the difference 3d(x²+y²) − 2d(x²+xy+y²) = d(x−y)².
The §15 claim (completed on the next page) that a degree >2 equation dx/X = dy/Y 'nullo amplius modo algebraice integrari posse' is false in general.
Counterexample to §15: X = x³ gives 1/x² − 1/y² = C.
Counterexample to §15: X = x³ − x gives ∫dx/X = ½ log((x²−1)/x²), hence the algebraic integral (x²−1)y²/(x²(y²−1)) = C.

The correct criterion: when X has only simple roots, an algebraic integral exists exactly when the residues of 1/X at those roots are rationally proportional. Multiple roots that bring in logarithms alongside rational parts block it.

Euler's own example 1+x³ is correctly transcendental, since its residues −r/3 are not commensurable. His caveat on the next page ('vnius generis tantum quantitates transcendentes') partly hedges the overstatement.
§14 shows only that this particular method fails, not impossibility.

ideas.what: Algebraic complete integral XY/(x−y)² = C of dx/X = dy/Y for quadratic X via Lagrange's dt-trick
ideas.modern_name: First integral of separated Riccati-type equation; Lagrange's method
ideas.where_published: E506 itself; similar integrals in Institutiones calculi integralis I

ideas.what: Completing to a square: (a+b(x+y)+cxy)/(x−y) = Δ, a symmetric bilinear relation giving y as a fractional linear function of x
ideas.modern_name: Möbius flow of a Riccati equation; polar form / cross-ratio invariant; degree-(1,1) analogue of Euler's symmetric biquadratic addition law
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (addition theorems); projective interpretation 19th c. (Cayley, Klein)
ideas.where_published: Euler's papers on comparing logarithms and circular arcs / addition theorems (e.g. Institutiones calculi integralis I); exact earlier locus unsure

ideas.what: The method breaks for cubic X, leaving the residual term d(x−y)²
Claim that degree >2 admits no algebraic integral
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic integrability of x' = X(x) (Liouville/Risch-type residue criterion)

missed.claim: Euler's general impossibility claim for degree >2 is false: dx/(x³−x) = dy/(y³−y) and dx/x³ = dy/y³ have algebraic complete integrals. The true condition is commensurability of the residues of 1/X. This is a minor overstatement, likely already noted in the Opera omnia commentary or easily seen; not a discovery.
missed.quote: talem aequationem differentialem, in qua vltra quadratum proceditur, nullo amplius modo algebraice integrari posse
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest as an early, imprecise statement of what Liouville-type residue criteria later settled.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine exposition of a known integral (Möbius/Riccati flow) and a standard limitation. The only notable point is an overstated impossibility claim, which is easily corrected and of minor historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'terminum dx³' / 'dy³' should be read as d·x³ and d·y³: d is a new constant coefficient, not a differential.
Previous page: '\frac{ddx}{dx\,dt}\,X'' is missing '=', and '\frac{dy}{dt}\,Y' is missing '='.
